🧑‍🔧 Who Runs the AI Factory · Overview

Who Runs the AI Factory at a Glance: 12 Layers, 12 Roles, One Machine

An AI factory is not only GPUs and power: it is a stack of software, and every layer has people who own it. This page brings the whole Who Runs the AI Factory series together: click any layer to see the role, the tools, what breaks and who they hand work to; find the roles that suit you; see how the jobs depend on each other; and follow one incident through the factory.

Explore the stack ↓ Find your role →
The stack Role finder Skills matrix Handoff web Follow one incident Career paths Real postings Reading tracks Glossary
⚠️ About this page. Every fact here comes from one of the twelve articles and inherits that article's sources and ⚠️ flags. Role descriptions are grounded in real job postings cited in each part (several may now be closed). Skill ratings, the role finder and the incident walkthrough are our editorial judgement and illustrations, not data. Nothing you click here is stored or sent anywhere.

🏭 The stack

Read from the bottom up: hardware becomes a cluster, the cluster runs training and data work, and the top layers serve, watch and protect what the factory produces.

🧭 Role finder

Five quick questions. We suggest the three roles that fit your answers best. Everything runs in your browser.

🧩 Skills matrix

How much each role leans on each skill, 1–5, distilled from the skill profiles in each part. Click a skill to sort roles by it.

🕸️ The handoff web

No layer works alone. Each line is a handoff described in the series. Click a role to highlight who it depends on and who depends on it.

🚨 Follow one incident

A composite scenario: a large training job slows down overnight. Watch how the problem moves through the roles until it is fixed.

🪜 Career paths

Common ways in, based on the backgrounds listed in each part's career box. Click a starting point.
